column1: # Candidate reference-genome IDENTITY list extracted from
# PlasBench's own truth_source=simulated track. Per this project's policy of
# never vendoring someone else's checked-in FASTA files, these rows carry
# only the IDENTITY of that repo's 20 reference genomes (organism/strain
# where the repo's own files state it, approximate genome size, and source
# study), extracted 2026-09-08 directly from that repo's own
# benchmarking_real.csv (6 rows, a subset re-using the same organisms with
# real instead of simulated reads -- not duplicated below), and
# benchmarking_simulate_demaio.csv (12 rows, De Maio et al.) -- see that
# repo's own README.md for the exact citation groupings. PlasBench downloads
# its OWN copy of each genome from NCBI once resolved, never the checked-in
# resolution -- this file is NOT yet valid input to
# sra_run). The repo's own CSVs give only an internal isolate identifier and
# an approximate genome size (its `-l`-style chromosome-length threshold for
# its own simulation step) -- NOT a BioSample or NCBI accession -- so a real
# per-genome NCBI search (organism/strain name -> BioSample -> assembly
# accession, the same chain resolve_ncbi_accessions.py already automates
# once a biosample is known) is a required, separate, NOT-YET-DONE step
# before this list can seed a real simulated cohort. Never fabricate a
# BioSample or accession here to skip that step.
# organism/strain is populated ONLY where the source repo's own filename
# states it explicitly (six of the eight Wick/Houtak/Mathers genomes below);
# "unconfirmed" means the repo's own files give an isolate identifier with
# no stated genus/species, and identifying it requires reading the actual
# cited paper (Wick et al., Houtak et al., Mathers et al., or De Maio et
# al. -- see source_study), not a guess from the identifier's shape alone.
